title: Portlight Ship Canon Entry
description: Schema for a named sailing vessel. Adapted from the Star Freight ship schema, which carried silhouette_cue + hull_repair_history + material_dominant as the heaviest trainable leverage. TWO ADDITIONS, both earned by a failed 2026-07-25 generation run that produced eight structurally inconsistent variants of one galleon: (1) `visual.rig_plan` enumerates masts and sails BY NAME, so a prompt can refer to 'the foremast' instead of 'one mast' and the model has a structural inventory to be consistent with. (2) `damage_ladder` declares which severity tiers the hull supports and what rig variants each produces — the tiers themselves are defined once in canon/damage-tiers.md, and which mast breaks is deliberately NOT scripted, because that is the judgement the anatomy training exists to produce. Both fields are freeze-watched.

id.description: Also the hull_id used by the portlight-ships pipeline and by every subject_id: <hull>__<state>__<rig>.

era.description: e.g. '1600s'. Keeps period drift out of the silhouette.

silhouette_cue.description: The read-at-a-glance shape. What makes this hull recognisable at sprite size.

palette.description: Required and pinned. An unpinned palette let the master's sails drift from the rest of the ladder.

rig_plan.description: The structural inventory. THIS IS THE FIX for part-level drift: masts and sails are NAMED, so prompts and damage states refer to specific objects rather than counts the model is free to reinvent.

sections.description: Lower / top / topgallant. A snapped mast breaks at a section join — naming them makes 'snapped partway up' unambiguous.

mast.description: id of the mast it is bent to, or 'bowsprit'.

rig_states.description: Orthogonal to damage. Star Freight had no sails, so this axis is new. 'sails-closed' means canvas FURLED — rolled and lashed along the yard, still present. It does NOT mean absent; a ship with no canvas is a stripped derelict.

damage_ladder.description:
Which severity tiers this hull supports, and what rig variants each tier produces. NOTHING MORE. The tiers themselves are defined once for the whole project in canon/damage-tiers.md.

Deliberately does NOT enumerate which mast breaks or which sail is lost. An earlier draft did, and that was hand-authoring the exact judgement the anatomy training exists to produce: a model that has learned a xebec's three lateen yards from pristine turnarounds should decide how they come down. Scripting it per hull means we never find out whether the training worked, and every new hull becomes an authoring job — which is the problem this pipeline was built to remove.

What canon still owes: that the tiers mean comparable severity across a sloop and a galleon, that damage never runs backwards, and that a tier whose canvas is destroyed cannot offer a furled variant.

rig_states.description: Which rig variants this tier produces. A tier whose canvas is destroyed cannot furl, so it offers sails-open only — that is WHY 04 has no closed variant, recorded rather than assumed.

hull_note.description: OPTIONAL, and only where this hull's tier genuinely departs from the shared definition — e.g. a single-masted vessel, where 'a mast is down' means something different. Not a place to re-script the damage.

forbidden_inputs.description: Negative constraints as CANON, written once, not rediscovered per prompt. Every entry here should trace to an observed failure.

signature_features.description: The identity anchors that must survive every damage state and every heading.
